html:
The ruined capital of the Vijayanagara empire, on the Tungabhadra river in Karnataka. It was founded in 1336 and by 1500 was among the largest and richest cities in the world.

It lies among hills of piled granite boulders, which gave it both stone and defence. Visitors from Persia and Portugal described seven rings of walls, markets selling jewels and horses, and crowds larger than in any city they knew. Under Krishnadevaraya it reached its height. Its best-known buildings are:

  • the Virupaksha temple, older than the city and still in use;
  • the Vittala temple, with a shrine in the shape of a stone chariot and pillars that ring when struck;
  • the royal quarter, with its elephant stables and stepped tanks.

In 1565 an alliance of the Deccan sultanates beat the Vijayanagara army at Talikota. The city was looted and burned over several months and never lived in again.
sum: The ruined capital of the Vijayanagara empire, on the Tungabhadra river in Karnataka. It was founded in 1336 and by 1500 was among the largest and richest cities in the world.
